name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Clostridium into several genera, of which Clostridium_A is one, so this page covers published work on Clostridium as a whole rather than on the GTDB subgroup alone.

sentences.text: Clostridium is described as the largest genus in the class Clostridia, made up of spore-forming, anaerobic, Gram-positive organisms.
Its members are reported to range from human pathogens to free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
A review describes the species placed in this genus as very heterogeneous phenotypically and phylogenetically, with several being reclassified into other genera as phylogeny advances.
The class Clostridia that contains this genus is described as a major microbial class of the human gut that ferments undigested carbohydrates and proteins into short-chain fatty acids.
